```{r setup-options, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4,
  out.width = "100%"
```

`geom_violinhist()` draws a half violin and a histogram side by side for
each group. The violin shows a smooth density estimate, while the
histogram shows the binned data it is based on, so you can judge both
the overall shape and how much data supports it.

```{r load-packages}
library(ggplot2)
library(sdlhRTools)
```

## Basic usage

Map a grouping variable to `x` and a continuous variable to `y`. By
default the violin is drawn on the right and the histogram on the left.

```{r basic}
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Width)) +
  geom_violinhist()
```

Mapping `fill` colours both halves by group:

```{r basic-fill}
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Width, fill = Species)) +
  geom_violinhist()
```

`geom_violinhist()` combines well with other layers, such as a narrow
boxplot and the raw points:

```{r combined}
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Width, fill = Species)) +
  geom_violinhist(binwidth = 0.3) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.05, fill = "white", outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(height = 0, width = 0.02, size = 0.8)
```

## Scaling groups: `scale`

The `scale` argument controls how groups are sized relative to each
other. It takes the same options as `ggplot2::geom_violin()` and applies
them to both halves. In all modes the largest group in the panel reaches
the full width, and the result does not depend on the units of `y`.

To see the differences, we use two small simulated datasets: one where
groups have the same shape but different sample sizes, and one where
groups have the same sample size but different spreads.

```{r sim-data}
set.seed(1)

# Same shape, different sample sizes
d_n <- data.frame(
  group = rep(c("small (n = 30)", "large (n = 300)"), c(30, 300)),
  y     = c(rnorm(30), rnorm(300))
)

# Same sample size, different spreads
d_sd <- data.frame(
  group = rep(c("narrow (sd = 0.5)", "wide (sd = 2)"), each = 200),
  y     = c(rnorm(200, sd = 0.5), rnorm(200, sd = 2))
)
```

### `"area"` (default)

Every group has the same area, regardless of how many observations it
has. Groups with the same distribution look the same even if one is ten
times larger, while a concentrated group is drawn wider than a
spread-out one.

```{r scale-area}
ggplot(d_n, aes(group, y, fill = group)) +
  geom_violinhist(binwidth = 0.5, scale = "area")

ggplot(d_sd, aes(group, y, fill = group)) +
  geom_violinhist(binwidth = 0.5, scale = "area")
```

### `"count"`

Areas are proportional to the number of observations, so smaller groups
are drawn smaller. Histogram bars are proportional to bin counts. Use
this when group size is part of the story.

```{r scale-count}
ggplot(d_n, aes(group, y, fill = group)) +
  geom_violinhist(binwidth = 0.5, scale = "count")
```

### `"width"`

Each group is scaled on its own so its peak reaches the full width. This
is useful for comparing the shapes of the distributions, but areas are
no longer comparable between groups.

```{r scale-width}
ggplot(d_sd, aes(group, y, fill = group)) +
  geom_violinhist(binwidth = 0.5, scale = "width")
```

### Different scaling for each half

`violin_scale` and `hist_scale` override `scale` for one half only. For
example, the violin can show group sizes while the histogram compares
shapes:

```{r scale-override}
ggplot(d_n, aes(group, y, fill = group)) +
  geom_violinhist(binwidth = 0.5, scale = "count", hist_scale = "area")
```

### Independent of units

Because bars are scaled against the largest group in the panel, changing
the units of `y` only changes the axis, not the plot:

```{r units}
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Width * 10, fill = Species)) +
  geom_violinhist(binwidth = 3) +
  labs(y = "Sepal.Width (mm)")
```

## Choosing bins: `bins` and `binwidth`

All groups share the same bins, so bars line up across groups, as in
`ggplot2::geom_histogram()`.

`bins` splits the full range of `y` into exactly that many equal bins.
The bin edges may fall on uneven values:

```{r bins}
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Width, fill = Species)) +
  geom_violinhist(bins = 12)
```

`binwidth` sets the width of each bin in the units of `y`, and places
bin edges at multiples of it. This usually gives rounder, easier-to-read
edges and is the recommended option:

```{r binwidth}
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Width, fill = Species)) +
  geom_violinhist(binwidth = 0.2)
```

## Layout: `side`, `hist_side_flip`, `nudge_value` and `width`

`side` chooses which side the violin is drawn on; the histogram goes on
the other side:

```{r side-left}
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Width, fill = Species)) +
  geom_violinhist(binwidth = 0.2, side = "left")
```

`hist_side_flip = TRUE` draws the histogram on the same side as the
violin, overlaid on it. A contrasting `hist_fill` keeps the bars visible
on top of the violin:

```{r side-flip}
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Width, fill = Species)) +
  geom_violinhist(binwidth = 0.2, hist_side_flip = TRUE, hist_fill = "grey20")
```

`nudge_value` moves the two halves apart, and `width` sets the maximum
length of the histogram bars in x-axis units:

```{r nudge-width}
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Width, fill = Species)) +
  geom_violinhist(binwidth = 0.2, nudge_value = 0.05, width = 0.3)
```

## Styling

The violin and the histogram are styled separately with the `violin_*`
and `hist_*` arguments. `fill` and `hist_fill` set fixed colours that
override any `fill` mapping:

```{r styling}
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Width)) +
  geom_violinhist(
    binwidth = 0.2,
    fill = "grey85",
    violin_linewidth = 0.3,
    hist_fill = "steelblue",
    hist_alpha = 0.8,
    hist_color = "white",
    hist_linewidth = 0.3
  )
```

It also works with the themes and palettes in this package:

```{r styling-package}
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Width, fill = Species)) +
  geom_violinhist(binwidth = 0.2, hist_alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_sdlh_d("paimio_contrast") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Sepal width (cm)") +
  theme_sdlh()
```

## Facets

Bins are shared across facets when the facet scales are fixed, so bars
can be compared between panels too:

```{r facets}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg, fill = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_violinhist(binwidth = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ am, labeller = as_labeller(c(`0` = "automatic", `1` = "manual"))) +
  labs(x = "cylinders", fill = "cylinders")
```

## Legends and inherited aesthetics

`show.legend` and `inherit.aes` apply to both halves. For example, to
hide the legend when `x` already identifies the groups:

```{r legend}
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Width, fill = Species)) +
  geom_violinhist(binwidth = 0.2, show.legend = FALSE)
```
